classification.distribution: Cultivated in suitable regions; distribution and legal cultivation are jurisdiction-dependent

identification.description: Annual herb with a glabrous, bluish-green appearance and characteristic poppy flower and capsule.
identification.whole_plant: Erect annual herb with a simple or sparsely branched stem and glaucous foliage.
identification.stem: Erect, smooth to sparsely hairy, often glaucous; upper portions bear flowers.
identification.leaf: Broad, lobed or toothed, glaucous leaves; upper leaves clasp the stem.
identification.flower: Large, showy flowers with four petals, commonly white, pink, purple or red depending on cultivar.
identification.fruit: Globose to ovoid capsule with a persistent stigmatic disc; diagnostic mature fruit structure.
identification.seed: Numerous small seeds within the capsule; colour varies by variety.
identification.bark: Not applicable as a distinct woody bark character.

dosha.vata: May pacify; classical and clinical context required

therapeutics.dose: Not supplied in this educational dossier; opioid-containing preparations require qualified professional supervision and applicable law.
therapeutics.precautions: Opium and opioid-containing preparations can cause dependence, respiratory depression, constipation and other serious adverse effects. Use only under qualified medical supervision and according to applicable regulations.
therapeutics.contraindications: Do not self-medicate with opium or opioid-containing preparations; contraindications depend on the preparation, patient and clinical context.

reference_hubs: TDU Indian Medicinal Plants Database — Shlokas

major_constituents: Opium alkaloids including morphine, codeine and papaverine
phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Alkaloid composition varies by plant material and processing. Pharmacologically active opioid constituents are clinically significant.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Papaver somniferum is the botanical source of opium and multiple opioid alkaloids. Modern clinical use is preparation-specific and regulated.
recognized_uses: Source plant for opioid and non-opioid alkaloids used in regulated pharmaceutical contexts
modern_information.safety_notes: This dossier is educational. It does not provide instructions for extraction, preparation, dosing or non-medical use.
sources: WHO opioid safety and medicines resources

exam_points: Characteristic capsule is an important identification feature
Latex is the traditionally recognized drug material; handling and use are legally regulated
viva_questions: Which family does Papaver somniferum belong to?
What is the characteristic fruit type used for identification?
Why does Ahiphena require special safety and regulatory consideration?
student.quick_revision: Ahiphena — Papaver somniferum L., Papaveraceae; annual glaucous herb with large flowers and characteristic capsule; latex is the traditionally recognized drug material and requires strict safety/regulatory control.

teaching_points: Demonstrate flower and capsule characters without handling controlled plant material.
Discuss the distinction between botanical identification and regulated medicinal use.
Explain why historical Ayurvedic terminology should be interpreted alongside modern pharmacology and regulation.
discussion_points: Traditional drug identity versus modern opioid pharmacology
practical_points: Use authenticated botanical images or herbarium material for identification; do not conduct extraction demonstrations.

doctor.quick_reference: Papaver somniferum-derived opioid material is clinically significant and regulated; therapeutic decisions are preparation-, patient- and jurisdiction-specific.
important_indications: Historical/traditional indications include Atisara, Pravahika and Vedana
key_precautions: Risk of respiratory depression and dependence
